correctness.rationale: Exact finite residual coefficients and Gramian are established by the cited 2019 theorem and also reconstructed via the moment constraints. Fixed-dimensional weighted-Hilbert matrix convergence gives every A_{j,L} scaling. Rational interpolation proves the nonzero first and last limits C_{beta,m}, D_{beta,m}. For alpha<0, two summations by parts and an o(1/L) total second-variation bound yield a uniform oscillatory terminal term. For alpha=0 the initial endpoint survives; for 0<alpha<1 the decreasing Dirichlet coefficients converge uniformly on closed-disk compacts away 1, and all j>=1 terms are lower order. Interior absolute convergence and nonzero constants give full claims. Finite numerical tests passed independently of the analytic proof. Boundaries: fixed m and alpha<1, away from z=1.

value.rationale: The explicit 2019 open boundary-uniformity gap for repeated zeros is a natural analytic problem not settled by the Hilbert-norm decay. The result covers every fixed multiplicity in the full alpha<1 coefficient scale and identifies a genuine alpha=0 transition in sharp boundary errors: terminal oscillation, two endpoints, or polylogarithmic initial-coefficient profile. Sharp constants, order rigidity, and the faster interior profile provide useful precise behavior for optimal polynomial inverses in Bergman/Dirichlet-type spaces; no paper-sized downstream theorem is required.
